# INDEX.md tables are generated by the BL-0025 docs generator in packages/backlog, and the standalone `index` check step is retired

**Date:** 2026-08-23  **Mode:** before  **Status:** active

## Question
BL-0032's last box makes each `packages/*/src/INDEX.md` file table generated from PS-057
file-purpose comments, spliced into a BL-0025 marker block. Two things need deciding: what
happens to the existing `index` step in `packages/check`
(`indexTable.ts` + `indexScan.ts` + the `index` branch in `run.ts`), and whether
`packages/backlog` — where `docsgen.ts` already lives — is the right home for INDEX.md
generation.

## Ruling
1. **Generation goes into the existing generator, in `packages/backlog`.** Extend
   `packages/backlog/src/docsgen.ts` (pure) and `packages/backlog/src/docsgenIo.ts` (IO).
   Do not create a package, do not add a second generator, and do not put a writer in
   `packages/check`.
2. **The `index` step is retired.** Delete `packages/check/src/indexTable.ts`,
   `packages/check/src/indexScan.ts`, `packages/check/test/indexTable.test.ts`, their
   re-exports in `packages/check/src/index.ts:12-14`, the `'index'` member of `StepName`,
   the `index` branch of `runStep`, `formatIndexIssue`, and `'index'` in `defaultSteps`.
   The `docs` step subsumes it.
3. **The gate still lives in `packages/check`.** `run.ts` remains the only definition of
   green; the `docs` step already invokes the generator as a subprocess
   (`run.ts:136`), so no new package import appears in either direction.
4. **The folder walker moves, it is not duplicated.** `scanIndexFolders`'s recursive
   discovery of source-bearing folders moves into the backlog IO layer (a new
   `docsgenIndex.ts` beside `docsgenIo.ts`, or `docsgenIo.ts` itself if it stays under
   ~200 lines). `packages/backlog` must not import `packages/check` to get it.
5. **`docs/decisions/2026-08-23-index-md-gate-owned-by-check.md` is superseded by this
   file.** Its live residue is carried forward here: `packages/check` must never import
   `packages/codemap`, enforced by `forbiddenEdges` in `packages/check/src/boundary.ts:23`.
   That rule stands unchanged.

## Because
- `regenerateDocs` (`packages/backlog/src/docsgenIo.ts:128`) already implements exactly the
  invariant the `index` step re-implements by hand: recompute the artifact, compare to what
  is committed, fail on difference. Keeping both leaves two gates asserting one invariant
  with different vocabularies (`IndexIssueKind` vs stale/unknown/missing block names).
- The `docs` check step runs `npx tsx packages/backlog/src/main.ts docs-regen --check`
  (`packages/check/src/run.ts:136`) — a subprocess, not an import. Moving generation to
  backlog therefore adds no edge to the module graph; `module_graph` shows
  `packages/backlog/src/*` importing only `packages/core` and itself.
- BL-0032's Bedrock (`backlog/BL-0032-src-folder-readme-index.md:117`) explicitly forbids
  building a second generator alongside BL-0025's. A generator in `packages/check` would be
  the second one.
- The three failure kinds the `index` step catches survive the move, but only if the
  generator is extended: `checkIndexFolder` (`packages/check/src/indexTable.ts:57`) fails on
  `missing-index`, `missing-entry`, `ghost-entry`, `empty-description`. Regeneration covers
  `missing-entry` and `ghost-entry` for free (the regenerated table differs from the
  committed one) and `empty-description` via the `missingDescriptions` pattern
  (`docsgen.ts:160`), but **not** `missing-index`: `regenerateDocs` returns
  `{stale: [], written: false}` when the target file does not exist (`docsgenIo.ts:140-142`),
  and a file with no marker block yields no stale names either. Both cases must become
  hard failures for INDEX.md targets, or retiring the step loses coverage.
- `docsTargets` is a fixed two-element list (`docsgenIo.ts:19`) and `buildBlocks` returns one
  global block map (`docsgen.ts:133`). INDEX.md targets are discovered from disk and each
  needs its own block body, so `regenerateDocs` must be generalized to per-target block maps.
  That is a refactor of the existing generator, which is what "not a second generator" means.
- `spliceBlocks` (`docsgen.ts:63`) leaves every byte outside a marker untouched and is
  documented idempotent, so the folder's own hand-written purpose paragraph above the table
  survives regeneration — which is what BL-0032's open box asks for.
- `StepName` escapes the package: `packages/mcp/src/dispatch.ts:43` names four steps
  (`typecheck`, `lint`, `ratchet`, `tests`) and does not name `index`, so removing the
  member breaks nothing there.
- The prior ruling's Ruling section states "the landed placement stands" and names files this
  change deletes. Leaving it `active` would leave two contradictory live rulings; its
  dependency-direction reasoning is preserved above and in `boundary.ts`, so nothing of value
  is lost by superseding it.

## Constraints for implementers
- Extend `packages/backlog/src/docsgen.ts` and `docsgenIo.ts`. No new package. No generator
  code in `packages/check`.
- `packages/backlog` must not gain an import of `packages/check` or `packages/codemap`. Move
  the folder-walk logic; do not import it.
- Generalize `regenerateDocs` to per-target block maps rather than adding a parallel
  `regenerateIndexes` entry point; `docsTargets` becomes "fixed targets plus discovered
  INDEX.md targets".
- Preserve all four failure modes of the retired step. Specifically, these must fail
  `docs-regen --check`: a source-bearing folder with no INDEX.md, an INDEX.md with no
  generated marker block, a `.ts` file with no PS-057 leading purpose comment, and a
  subfolder whose INDEX.md has no opening purpose statement.
- Harvesting stays lexical: read the leading `//` comment block of the file as text. Do not
  reach for `packages/codemap` or the TypeScript API to get it.
- Use one marker name in every INDEX.md (e.g. `src-index`) rather than encoding the folder
  path in the marker, so a folder rename does not invalidate the block.
- Delete, in the same change, `indexTable.ts`, `indexScan.ts`, `test/indexTable.test.ts`, the
  three re-export lines in `packages/check/src/index.ts`, and every `'index'` occurrence in
  `run.ts` (`StepName`, the `Exclude<>` in `commands`, the `runStep` branch,
  `formatIndexIssue`, `defaultSteps`). Leaving a dead step name is the failure mode here.
- Regenerating twice must produce byte-identical output on a CRLF working tree; `detectEol`
  (`docsgen.ts:54`) exists for this and must be honoured for the new targets. Add a test.
- Update `packages/check/src/INDEX.md` rows 11-13 and `packages/backlog/src/INDEX.md` in the
  same change — they describe the files being deleted and added.

## Rejected
- **Keep both gates.** Two mechanisms for one invariant; they will diverge on the first new
  failure kind, and the `index` step's `empty-description` becomes unreachable once
  descriptions are harvested rather than typed.
- **Put the generator in `packages/check`, reusing `indexScan.ts`.** `check` is the gate
  runner and owns no writers; `docs-regen --write` writes files. It would also be the second
  generator BL-0032's Bedrock forbids.
- **New `packages/docs` package for generation.** A package costs a manifest, a tsconfig
  entry, an INDEX.md, and a map row to move ~300 lines that have one consumer. Cheap to do
  later if a third consumer appears; expensive to undo now.
- **Move `docsgen*.ts` out of `packages/backlog` first, then extend it.** Correct in the long
  run — doc generation is not backlog parsing — but it puts a package-shaped refactor in
  front of a blocked feature. The map row is amended instead so the doctrine stops
  understating what the package owns.
- **Keep `indexTable.ts` as a library the generator imports.** Would create a
  `backlog -> check` edge for parsing that the generator no longer needs: it writes the
  table, so it never has to parse one.

## Enforcement
Partly mechanical. The freshness invariant is enforced by the `docs` step itself. The
dependency constraints are enforceable today by adding two rows to `forbiddenEdges` in
`packages/check/src/boundary.ts:23`: `packages/backlog -> packages/check` and
`packages/backlog -> packages/codemap`. Both are worth filing — the boundary step already
exists, so each is a one-line addition plus a test.

## Revisit when
A third consumer of the marker-block generator appears, or `docsgen*.ts` grows past the
backlog-parsing code it sits beside — either is the trigger to move doc generation out of
`packages/backlog` into its own package.
